findings.title: Second `def self.downsize` overrides the 5-arg one; ResizeEmoji job now raises ArgumentError
findings.body: Ruby has no overloading. `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149 replaces `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 145, so the first definition is dead. The existing caller `app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14` still calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)`. That is 5 arguments against a method that now takes at most 4, so it raises `ArgumentError`. Every custom-emoji upload that enqueues `Jobs::ResizeEmoji` then fails, and the emoji is never downsized to 100x100. The same file shows the problem: line 146 is unreachable. Fix by keeping a single `downsize`. Either change it to the `dimensions` form and update `resize_emoji.rb` to pass `"100x100"`, or give the new string-dimension variant a different name. `resize` at line 142 only had its internals changed, so it is fine.

findings.title: Hard-coded 10MB client limit replaces max_attachment_size_kb / max_image_size_kb
findings.body:
The client check used to read `max_<type>_size_kb`, so it covered both images and attachments. It is now a constant 10MB for everything. Two consequences:
1. An admin who set `max_attachment_size_kb` above 10MB (for example the `script/import_scripts/tnation.rb:115-116` style settings) can no longer upload attachments larger than 10MB, because the client refuses them. The `max_attachment_size_kb` setting is silently capped.
2. An attachment between `max_attachment_size_kb` and 10MB is no longer caught on the client. The whole file is uploaded before the server rejects it, which is a worse experience than before. Only images should get the relaxed limit, since only images are downsized server-side. Keep `max_attachment_size_kb` for `type === 'attachment'` and use the larger bound for images.

The same constant is repeated at line 246 for the 413 message, and at `uploads_controller.rb:55` for API URL downloads, which also ignores `max_attachment_size_kb`.

Tests: `test/javascripts/lib/utilities-test.js.es6:52-61` ("prevents files that are too big from being uploaded") sets `max_image_size_kb = 5` and a 10KB file, then expects `file_too_large` with `max_size_kb: 5`. With this change the file passes validation and the message would say 10240, so that test will fail. It needs updating, and a test is needed for the new limit.

findings.title: Downsize with "80%" is unsupported for animated GIFs, and the result is ignored
findings.body: With `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails`, `OptimizedImage.optimize` (`optimized_image.rb:155`) switches to `downsize_instructions_animated` when the path matches `/\.GIF$/i`. That calls `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%` (`optimized_image.rb:120`), and `--resize-fit` expects `WxH`, not a percentage. The command fails and `convert_with` returns false. The loop at lines 66-69 ignores the return value, so it runs 5 no-op attempts and the file stays oversized. The user then gets whatever size error the validator raises, instead of an automatic downsize. If the tempfile path has no `.gif` extension, `convert ...[0]` is used instead, which keeps only the first frame, so animation is lost without notice. Check the return value (break on false). For GIFs, either use a size gifsicle accepts or skip animation handling deliberately. There is also no spec for the new downsizing behaviour in `spec/controllers/uploads_controller_spec.rb`.

contracts.action: Controller downsizes oversized images before Upload.create_for
contracts.equivalent_path: Upload.create_for resize for cropped image types (app/models/upload.rb:82-99), which also calls OptimizedImage.resize in place on file.path
contracts.before_after: Before: an image over max_image_size_kb was rejected by the validator. After: up to 5 in-place `convert -resize 80%>` passes run on the tempfile first, and the new size is passed to create_for.
contracts.visible_effect: Large images are accepted at reduced size. If downsizing fails (GIF with gifsicle and a percentage), the upload still fails with a size error and no downsize happens.
contracts.failure_mode: convert_with returns false, which the loop ignores and retries 5 times. The tempfile is closed in `ensure` (line 85) either way.

contracts.before_after: Before: the 5-arg form was accepted. After: only the (from, to, dimensions, opts) form exists, so the 5-arg call raises ArgumentError.
contracts.visible_effect: Custom emoji are no longer resized to 100x100 after upload.
contracts.failure_mode: The background job raises ArgumentError on each run.

summary: Not safe to merge as is. The duplicate `OptimizedImage.downsize` definition makes the second one win, so the unchanged `ResizeEmoji` job passes 5 arguments and raises ArgumentError. The hard-coded 10MB client limit also overrides `max_attachment_size_kb`, and it breaks the existing JS spec that expects the `max_image_size_kb` limit. The controller's `\"80%\"` downsize is not supported for animated GIFs, and its result is ignored. I read all three files and the callers I cite; I did not run anything.
